fields.meta_title: Painting Quote Form That Prices Each Room | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a painting quote form that prices each room, takes photos, sends big exterior jobs to an estimator, and saves every request. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Painting Quote Form Customers Fill Out Room by Room
fields.hero_description: Build a painting quote form that prices each room from your rates and saves every request to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Painter Needs Before Pricing the Job
fields.features_subheading: A painting quote form replaces the walk-through for small jobs. The customer lists rooms, surfaces, and photos, and the price follows.
fields.feature_1:
A price that follows the room list

Set a rate for each kind of room and an add-on for ceilings or trim. As the customer adds rooms, the form totals the quote, and the price shown is the one saved with the request.
fields.feature_2:
Photos attached to the right wall

Give each room or side of the house its own upload field. Peeling trim, water stains, and old wallpaper reach the estimator with the room they belong to, not in a text thread.
fields.feature_3:
Jobs that need a visit go to a person

Write the rule for jobs you will not price online, such as 3 stories or more. Those requests skip the price and go to the estimator you name, by email or in Slack, with the photos.
fields.feature_4:
Counts for doors, drawers, and windows

Cabinet and trim work price by the piece. Ask for the number of doors, drawer fronts, or window frames, set a rate for each, and the quote shows every line with its count and price.
fields.feature_5:
A signature that accepts the quote

Show the customer every line and the total, then a signature box and an accept button. The app saves the signature and the signing date with the accepted quote in a database you own.
fields.feature_6:
The whole app in your GitHub

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository. Run the quote form on your own servers and connect it to the scheduling or accounting tools your crews already use.
fields.why_title: Why Build Painting Quote Forms With Emergent?

fields.tab_content_1:
All 3 rooms and both ceilings, priced at $1,880

Odessa Varnell wants 3 rooms repainted. On the Brushline Painting form she adds 2 bedrooms at $480 each and a living room at $640. She checks the ceiling box in both bedrooms, at $140 each. The form shows $1,880 before she submits, and the request lands in Brushline's table with her address.
fields.tab_content_2:
Any house of 3 stories or more goes to Clemency

Ravelstone Exteriors prices one- and two-story houses online. Any house of 3 stories or more goes to estimator Clemency Wroxley for a site visit. Ezekiel Corwick's house has 3 stories and peeling trim on the north side. He uploads a photo of each of the 4 sides, and Clemency gets an email with all 4 and the address.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each door at $85 and each drawer front at $45

Marisela Pevensey is painting her kitchen cabinets instead of replacing them. Finchwood Cabinet Painting's form prices each door at $85 and each drawer front at $45. Her 22 doors and 9 drawer fronts come to $2,275. She signs on her phone to accept, and the signature is saved with the quote.
fields.tab_content_4:
Lowell gets each room's color on May 10, 2 days early

Pennbrook Painting offers 24 wall colors, each with a name and a number. Cosima Bartlett picks one for each of her 4 rooms, such as Fog Linen, number 112, for the den. The app saves her picks by room. Crew lead Lowell Ravensby gets the color sheet by email on May 10, 2 days before the May 12 start.

How do I create a painting quote form?

plan.angle: Results for this query are printable estimate templates and pricing guides. This page shows a painting quote form as the request a painter prices from: interior rooms priced from the painter's own rates, exterior jobs of 3 stories or more routed to an estimator with photos of each side, cabinet doors and drawer fronts counted and signed for, and wall colors picked by room for the crew lead. Pricing averages and color advice are left out; the one outside fact is the EPA's pre-1978 lead-safe certification rule, quoted with its own limits.
